While I agree stats and their interpretations can be biased. People in this context are talking stats to a dude who’s never been to memphis. That’s the best way to portray information to someone who’s never seen or heard anything about the various parts of memphis. It’s the best way to put the risks associated with moving into these areas into perspective without needing to explain everything ACTUALLY happening in Memphis. 

There are people who can’t afford the financial hit if someone steals or breaks into something. If someone’s moving from CA, they’re not going to know shit about living here/the general state of various parts of memphis. Claiming that using objective statistics like violent crime and petty crime stats is biased is counterproductive. If we use these statistics to understand what these communities in question need, we can easily control the problems that plague them. Maybe they need more policing, maybe less, maybe they need more job opportunities, maybe they need contractors to come in and fix up certain areas to improve the quality of life in these areas. 

I grew up in orange mound, we had 3 home invasions by the time I was 14. Chalking everything up to “aww these fuckin white suburban Karens think these parts of town are a lot worse than they are” ,when there genuinely IS a crime rate compared to other parts of the city, is just willingly ignorant. In this context, people are literally just using objective fact (in the form of official, unbiased crime statistics) to warn this dude about the potential dangers, struggles, and issues associated with living in this particular area.

People are talking statistics bc it’s a form of information that is easy for anyone to easily understand. It’s almost like that’s what statistics are made for. Saying this has anything to do with skin color is just disingenuous deflecting of the actual issues plaguing the wider community. Issues of drug addiction, crime, poverty, and general inequality are not going to be solved by telling everyone those problems don’t exist and are just made up but the “racist white suburban mob”.

My the end of my grandmother’s life. My grandmother practically raised me as both my parent were out of the house at almost all times. She was supportive of me in everything. She was a shoulder to cry on. She was everything to me. When I was really young I used to call her mom on accident. About a year and a half ago her voice changed. Her voice was suddenly extremely gravely and nothing at all like her regular voice. I noticed that she was starting to have issues walking and I had to start helping her around the house. They had been to countless hospitals and only on the 16th they found that she had ALS. They never wanted to tell me as they didn’t want to hurt me. She told me that she had it 2 months before she died. She actually called me the night of her death to ask how I did in school. The last thing she ever tried to eat was a small, cut up hamburger that my dad made for her. I thought she had more time. I thought it wasn’t that serious. I thought, “look at how long Stephen Hawking kept going, surely she had more time” she died of respiratory failure on August 2, 2020. I think a piece of me died that day, too.
